title: Herding knowledge and config docs carry herdr's lifecycle contract
action: Record herdr's agent lifecycle contract in the knowledge layer and retire every statement of the behavior herding-prompt-stall D1 and D2 replace. CONTEXT.md quotes the contract verbatim from `herdr --skill`; cite it, do not paraphrase it loosely. What must land: (a) the five states and what each one means to bee — `idle` is ready-for-input AND the tab has been seen in the focused Herdr UI; `done` is the SAME underlying ready state for a tab nobody has looked at, and since bee splits every worker pane with `--no-focus` and only ever reads over the CLI (which never marks a tab seen), `done` is the normal resting state of a bee worker pane; `blocked` means herdr recognized an approval or question UI; `unknown` does not prove completion. (b) That a lifecycle sample taken inside the agent's boot window is not trustworthy — an agy pane flaps through several states while its TUI initializes — which is why bee now uses herdr's own settle-aware verbs (`agent prompt --wait --until … --timeout`, `agent wait --until …`) instead of polling raw samples, and why herdr's `agent_prompt_stalled` is the delivery failure. (c) That `blocked` is bee's fast, loud failure at every wait point, and that this is what covers a per-workspace trust or approval prompt without bee carrying an agent-specific pattern table. Search both files for any surviving claim that the ready gate is idle-only or that the delivery receipt is a transition into `working`, and replace each with the new rule naming the superseding decision inline so a later reader does not resurrect it. Do not restructure either document, renumber anything, or touch the agent-registry (`herding.agents`) sections — those are correct and out of scope.
verify: rg -n 'idle-only|transition into working|idle only' docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/ skills/bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md; rg -n 'blocked|agent_prompt_stalled|done' skills/bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md
